title: introduce credential templates + compact resumable pullstream; align SDK streaming APIs
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: tri-SDK parity drift caused subtle auth window and stream-resume incompatibilities for customers running cross-language clients. This PR introduces a small, opinionated Credential Template Registry plus a compact resumable pullstream shim and synchronizes streaming surface area across Python/TypeScript/Go to reduce footguns and enable ergonomic migration.

Summary of changes: checklist: [x] introduce CredentialTemplate registry (py/ts/go) and builder helpers; [x] implement compact resumable Pullstream shim with explicit resume token semantics; [x] unify streaming chunk/event shape and backpressure hooks across SDKs; [x] add migration docs and changelogs; [x] bump SDK package versions and CI matrix.

Design notes: credential templates are a small typed surface that lets consumers declare credential composition (api_key, delegated_token, kms_wrapped) and retry profiles in a single object. Implementations in each SDK normalize TTL jitter and expose a consistent .refresh() lifecycle hook used by the streaming shim. The Pullstream shim is intentionally minimal: it exposes resume(token) and checkpoint() primitives and a RetryPredicate interface so platform teams can plug circuit/backoff heuristics without reauthoring stream code.

Compatibility & rollout: default behavior is backwards-compatible; existing credential providers continue to work. The template registry is opt-in; we provide an adapter to wrap legacy providers. The new pullstream shim preserves the old async-iterable and readable-stream surfaces but adds an explicit resume API. We ran a staged rollout: canary (internal) -> beta customers -> full release.

Testing: added unit tests across all three SDKs (credential lifecycle, resume semantics, backpressure handshake), integration tests that exercise cross-language resume by running a TypeScript producer and Python consumer in the test harness, and e2e scenarios against local private deployer (redwood-private-installer test stack). CI matrix exercised py3.9/3.11, node 16/18, go1.20/1.22.

Docs & migration: included a short migration guide (docs/sdk-migration.md) with examples for migrating from legacy token refresh loops to CredentialTemplate+registry. Changelogs updated with recommended upgrade path and examples.

Rollback plan: switch consumers back to legacy credential adapter via env var REDWOOD_SDK_LEGACY_CRED=true; teardown guard added to SDK initializers.

Related: ENG-9281 (credential consistency), ENG-9310 (stream parity), SUP-1123 (customer incident referencing stale resume tokens).

review_comments: Sanjay Patel (reviewer): This looks solid — can we make the retry predicate pluggable without exposing too many internals? I left a small nit on the Go interface naming.
Maya Chen (author): Good call — extracted predicate as RetryPredicate interface and added a factory with sane defaults. Updated Go naming per suggestion.
Diego Marquez (reviewer): The TS streaming tests flaked once in CI; can we add a stabilizing sleep or a better synchronization? Also consider documenting the latency tradeoff on resume().

Maya Chen (author): Reworked the TS test to use an explicit readiness signal (test harness channel) instead of time.Sleep; added a short note in the migration doc about potential tails under heavy batching.
Evelyn Wu (approver): Verified cross-language integration locally and ran the private-installer e2e. Approving — please squash and include a concise release note.
CI Bot: e2e job rerun after flaky failure — all checks passed on second run.
release_notes: Added a Credential Template Registry (opt-in) and a compact resumable pullstream shim across Python/TypeScript/Go. These changes improve stream resume semantics and standardize credential lifecycle hooks; migration guide and adapters included. Bumped SDK versions: python 0.10.0, typescript 1.28.0, go 1.5.0.
testing_summary: unit tests (py/ts/go), cross-lang integration job, local private-installer e2e; CI matrix expanded
rationale: Reduce tri-sdk parity drift and provide a low-friction path to robust resume/retry semantics for streaming workloads.
